title: Facebook Ads – How They Work, How Much They Cost, and How to Set Them Up
excerpt: Facebook advertising is paid promotion in the Meta Ads ecosystem. See how the ad auction works, what campaigns cost, how Ads Manager differs from boosting posts, and how to set up an effective campaign step by step.
metaDescription: How do Facebook ads work, what do they cost, and how do you set them up in Ads Manager? Campaign objectives, targeting, budgets, CPM and CPC, optimization, and the most common mistakes.

runs.text: What is Facebook advertising?

Facebook advertising is a paid form of promotion in the Meta Ads ecosystem that lets you reach users of Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, and the Audience Network. It serves sales, lead generation, traffic growth, brand awareness, and remarketing.

Meta Ads is Meta's advertising system, covering Facebook Ads and Instagram Ads among others. The advertiser creates ad campaigns and defines the objective, ad budget, audiences, ad format, and placements.
A well-planned Facebook ad is not about boosting a post at random. It's a process in which strategy, data, ad creatives, and campaign optimization all work toward a specific business result.
How do Facebook ads work in the Meta Ads system?

Ads run through an auction-based delivery system in which Facebook's algorithm picks who sees your ad, weighing the campaign objective, budget, ad quality, target audience, and the odds of the desired action being taken.
In practice this means Meta doesn't show ads randomly. The system analyzes user behavior, demographics, activity history, and conversion probability.
If the campaign objective is sales, Facebook's algorithm looks for people similar to those who buy. If the objective is traffic, ads go to users likely to click the link.
Why does effective Facebook advertising need the right campaign objective?

The campaign objective decides which action the Meta Ads system optimizes delivery for. A campaign set up for sales works differently than one for leads, traffic, engagement, brand awareness, or app promotion.
The choice of objective affects cost, traffic quality, and campaign performance. A mistake at this stage means your ad budget works toward the wrong actions.
Effective Facebook advertising starts with answering one question: what should users do after seeing the ad? Buy a product, submit a form, visit a website, or remember the brand.
How to set up a Facebook ad step by step?
To run a Facebook ad you need a fan page, an ad account, access to Business Manager, a campaign objective, a budget, a target audience, a creative, placements, and a way to measure results.

First, prepare the business page, the ad account, and Business Manager. Then choose the objective, a daily or lifetime budget, the schedule, audiences, and ad format. The next stage is configuring the ad itself: copy, headline, image, video, CTA button, and destination URL. In sales campaigns, the Meta Pixel, the Conversions API, and correctly set up events on your website all matter.
Companies that don't want to burn their budget on unplanned tests often turn to specialists in <a0>running Facebook ad campaigns</a0>, especially when the goal is sales, leads, or scaling.
How is Ads Manager different from boosting posts?

Ads Manager gives you full control over the campaign, budget, objective, target audience, placements, and measurement. Boosting posts is a simplified option, fine for basic reach but strategically limited.
Boosting posts works fast, but it doesn't unlock Facebook's full advertising toolkit. Conversion optimization, A/B tests, remarketing, and advanced targeting options are harder to control.

Facebook Ads Manager lets you build effective paid campaigns split into ad sets and creatives. It's the right tool when Facebook advertising is meant to support sales, lead acquisition, and a measurable return on investment.
How to choose a target audience for Facebook Ads campaigns?
A target audience is the set of users your ads are shown to. It should follow from your product, the stage of the sales funnel, customer data, location, user behavior, and the campaign objective.

For an online store, people ready to buy are one audience and users just getting to know the brand are another. Facebook Ads campaigns should separate cold traffic, remarketing, and existing customers. It pays to analyze data from your CRM, website, forms, sales, and social media. The more a company knows about its users, the better it targets its ads.
What does precise targeting on Facebook make possible?
Precise targeting lets you reach audiences by location, age, gender, interests, behaviors, first-party data, custom audiences, and lookalike audiences.
Custom audiences can be built from website visits, fan-page activity, customer lists, video views, and ad interactions. That's the foundation of remarketing.

Lookalike audiences help you find new customers similar to the people who already bought, submitted a form, or completed another valuable action. That's how Meta campaigns can scale sales without pure guesswork.
Which Facebook ad formats are worth testing?

Campaigns should test ad formats such as single image, video ads, carousel ads, collections, and dynamic creative. The format should fit the product, the stage of the purchase journey, and audience behavior.

Video ads are good at showing a service, a process, a before-and-after, or a customer review. Carousel ads present several products, benefits, or offer stages in one ad. The best ads come from testing, not from a single idea. Compare creatives, headlines, the opening sentence, CTAs, copy length, and message layout.
How much does Facebook advertising cost?

Facebook advertising costs as much as the advertiser puts into the budget, but real results depend on the industry, competition, seasonality, creative quality, target audience, campaign objective, and landing page.
A test campaign can start at around 20–30 zł a day. That budget gathers the first data, but it isn't always enough for stable sales or a larger volume of leads.

In Poland, a typical CPC falls between 1 zł and 8 zł, depending on the industry and how competitive it is. What costs money is effective advertising, not the click itself, so judge CPA, ROAS, and conversion quality.
How much do 1,000 Facebook ad impressions cost?
The cost of 1,000 Facebook ad impressions is captured by CPM. Its level depends on auction competition, creative appeal, audience quality, seasonality, campaign objective, and placements.
CPM shows what the advertiser pays for a thousand ad impressions. A low CPM doesn't automatically mean success if the ad generates no clicks, leads, or sales.
In sales campaigns, ROAS, CPA, and conversions matter more than CPM alone. Cheap impressions with no user response don't build a business result.
How much does Facebook pay for 1,000 views?

Facebook doesn't pay the advertiser for 1,000 impressions of a standard ad. In Facebook Ads campaigns it's the advertiser who pays — for delivery, clicks, conversions, or other actions defined by the campaign objective.
Asking how much FB pays per 1,000 views is really a question about creator monetization, not classic ad campaigns. Those are two different mechanisms.
In online advertising, a company invests a budget to win traffic, contacts, or sales. The return shows up when the campaign generates more revenue than the advertising costs.
How to measure ad campaign performance?
Campaign performance is measured with metrics tied to the business goal: ROAS, CPA, CPC, CPM, CTR, conversion count, cost per lead, cart value, and website traffic quality.

ROAS is the return on ad spend. CPA is the cost of acquiring an action, such as a purchase or a form submission. CPC shows the cost per click, CPM the cost per thousand impressions, and CTR how well the ad draws attention.
The number of likes alone isn't enough. Effective ad campaigns should answer whether the ads bring in potential customers and support sales growth.
How to optimize Facebook Ads campaigns?
Campaign optimization means regularly analyzing data, switching off weak ads, reinforcing strong ad sets, testing creatives, refining audiences, and improving the landing page.

Ongoing optimization covers cost control, frequency, traffic quality, and conversions. If CTR drops, the creative is often the problem. If clicks don't sell, the problem sits with the offer, the landing page, or the events.
A/B tests compare headlines, images, video, messaging, and audiences. They let you build effective ads on data rather than intuition.
Which mistakes hurt ad performance most often?

The most common mistakes: the wrong campaign objective, a too-broad or random target audience, weak creatives, no conversion measurement, skipped remarketing, a test budget that's too small, and judging results by likes.

Another problem is pouring the whole budget into a single ad. Without tests it's hard to tell whether a weak result comes from the image, the copy, the offer, the price, the audience, or the landing page.
Many companies never install the Meta Pixel and the Conversions API. The Facebook algorithm then has less data to work with, and campaign optimization performs worse.
When is it worth handing campaigns to specialists?

It's worth outsourcing campaigns when a company spends its budget without stable results, doesn't measure conversions, wants to scale sales, lower CPA, improve ROAS, or tie advertising into a broader digital marketing strategy.

A specialist analyzes more than the Facebook ads themselves: the offer, the landing page, the sales funnel, the data, and lead quality. Paid campaigns then become part of a sales system instead of a separate activity.

How to combine Facebook Ads with social media management?
Facebook Ads and social media management should work together: ads amplify reach, while consistent communication builds recognition, trust, brand context, and more effective sales funnels.

A profile without ads grows more slowly, and ads without coherent communication lose credibility. Facebook users often check a brand out before buying, so organic content affects campaign performance.

Social Lama combines advertising with social media communication. That way <a0>social media management</a0> supports the ads, and the ads amplify the content that builds relationships with your audience.
Is Facebook advertising still worth it?

Facebook advertising still pays off when it has a clear objective, a correct setup, a well-chosen audience, attractive creatives, reliable conversion measurement, and regular optimization. Without a strategy it quickly becomes a cost.

Facebook remains a strong channel for e-commerce, local businesses, services, education, lead recruitment, and brand awareness. Its strengths are data, scale, and the option to pair campaigns with Instagram. The best results go to companies that treat Meta Ads as a process. What counts is testing, analysis, scaling, and consistently improving every element of the campaign.
Summary

Facebook advertising is a tool for winning customers, driving sales, generating leads, and building brand awareness. It performs best when run through Ads Manager rather than through post boosting alone. Costs depend on the industry, competition, creatives, and campaign objective, so measure not just clicks but also CPA, ROAS, and conversions. Effective advertising takes data, testing, remarketing, and ongoing optimization.
FAQ – frequently asked questions
How much does Facebook advertising cost?
Ads can start at around 20–30 zł a day during the test phase. The real cost depends on the industry, competition, campaign objective, creative quality, and target audience.
How to set up a Facebook ad?
You need a fan page, an ad account, and access to Business Manager. Then you pick the campaign objective, budget, target audience, ad format, placements, and how results will be measured.
Is boosting posts enough?
Boosting posts is enough for a simple bump in reach or engagement. For sales, leads, remarketing, and conversion optimization, Meta Ads Manager is the better tool.
